newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin says Thai baht undervalued.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin says Thai baht undervalued.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Virawan said on Tuesday that the baht was still undervalued contrary to some analysts' views that it was overvalued.

"Many analysts say that the baht is not at a level where it is overvalued. Many think instead that it is undervalued," he said while making a policy statement to a gathering of businessmen and bankers at his ministry.
The Thai baht came under attack by offshore speculators on Monday and Tuesday as it dropped against the rising dollar on active selling, especially in the Singapore market.
Dealers said demand for dollars from companies for year-end book squaring also pushed the baht down.
They said the Bank of Thailand had intervened in the market to defend the baht by selling dollars in Singapore.

Amnuay did not comment directly on the baht attack. But he said he would try to maintain the stability of the baht and ruled out the consideration of any change in the baht fixing policy in the near term.
"There would be no consideration of the baht policy right now. We are confident that we will be able to maintain the stability of the baht (under the current system)," he said.
After his comments, the baht stabilised somewhat to 25.590-25.595 against the dollar at 0759 GMT after sliding to a low of 25.612 earlier in the day.
The central bank currently fixes the daily value of the baht against major currencies by using a basket of currencies, heavily weighted in the dollar.
The Finance Minister said the policy of making the baht more flexible would be considered later by relevant agencies when the need arises.
